sections.title: Executive Summary + Investment Thesis
sections.body:
**Executive Summary + Investment Thesis**

Infosys, a leading technology services company, has demonstrated robust financial performance, with 6.1% revenue growth and a 21.1% operating margin in the reported period. The company's strong cash generation capabilities, evident from its 44.8% free cash flow growth, have enabled it to maintain a debt-free and liquid balance sheet. As of March 31, 2025, the company's financial position is characterized by a robust cash and investments portfolio, with a focus on prudent business decisions to deliver long-term growth. 

Our investment thesis is centered on Infosys' ability to deliver sustainable and profitable growth, driven by its strategic focus on scale agile digital and core business energization. With a high return on equity of 29.0% and a commitment to returning approximately 85% of its free cash flow to shareholders over a five-year period, Infosys presents an attractive investment opportunity. The company's strong credit rating, AAA as per CRISIL, and its access to capital markets further reinforce its financial stability. While specific details on net profit and net worth are not provided in the excerpts, Infosys' overall financial performance and capital allocation policy suggest a positive outlook for investors.

sections.title: Business Overview + Segment Breakdown
sections.body:
INFY's business is diversified across various segments, including Financial Services, Retail, Communication, Energy, Utilities, Resources and Services, Manufacturing, Hi-Tech, Life Sciences, and All other segments. The company's revenue from operations for the year ended March 31, 2025, was ₹1,62,990 crore, with the Financial Services segment contributing ₹45,175 crore, followed by Retail at ₹22,059 crore, and Communication at ₹19,108 crore. The All other segments, which include operating segments of businesses in India, Japan, China, Infosys Public Services, and other enterprises in Public Services, accounted for ₹4,810 crore of revenue from operations.

The segment-wise breakdown of revenue and identifiable operating expenses for the years ended March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, is provided in the financial statements. The Financial Services segment had identifiable operating expenses of ₹25,871 crore and allocated expenses of ₹8,205 crore for the year ended March 31, 2025. The segment operating income for Financial Services was ₹11,099 crore, while the total segment operating income for all segments was ₹39,236 crore. The company's net profit for the year ended March 31, 2025, was ₹26,750 crore, with a depreciation and amortization expense of ₹4,812 crore. No client individually accounted for more than 10% of the revenues for the year ended March 31, 2025.

sections.title: Financial Performance
sections.body:
The 'Financial Performance' section of this report is based on the provided filing excerpts from the Infosys Integrated Annual Report 2024-25. According to the report, the company achieved a revenue growth of 6.1% and maintained an operating margin of 21.1%. The return on equity stood at 29.0%, indicating a strong profitability position. The company also reported a robust free cash flow growth of 44.8%, with free cash flow defined as net cash provided by operating activities less capital expenditure. As of the reporting date, the company's consolidated cash and investments position was not explicitly stated in the provided excerpts, but it was mentioned that the company remains debt-free and maintains adequate cash to meet operational and strategic requirements.

The company's financial performance is also reflected in its dividend payout policy, with a stated intention to return approximately 85% of the free cash flow cumulatively over a five-year period through a combination of semi-annual dividends and/or share buyback/special dividends. The dividend per share growth was reported at 13.2%, excluding special dividends. However, specific numbers for revenue from operations, net profit, and net worth are not provided in the excerpts, limiting a more comprehensive analysis of the company's financial performance.

sections.title: Balance Sheet Health + Cash Flow
sections.body:
The balance sheet of Infosys remains debt-free, with a strong focus on maintaining liquidity to meet operational and strategic requirements. As of the latest available data, the company's primary sources of liquidity are cash and cash equivalents, as well as cash flow generated from operations. Infosys also holds investments in liquid mutual funds, fixed maturity plan securities, commercial paper, and other high-credit-rated instruments, guided by its treasury policy. The company's consolidated cash and investments are comprised of deposits in banks, investments in liquid mutual funds, and other financial instruments. 

In terms of cash flow, Infosys has demonstrated strong cash generation capabilities, with free cash flow growth of 44.8% as per the latest available data. The company defines free cash flow as net cash provided by operating activities less capital expenditure, as per the Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows prepared under IFRS. Effective from the financial year 2025, Infosys expects to continue its policy of returning approximately 85% of the free cash flow cumulatively over a five-year period through a combination of semi-annual dividends and/or share buyback/special dividends, subject to applicable laws and requisite approvals. However, specific numbers on the company's net worth, cash, and cash equivalents are not provided in the available excerpts.

sections.title: Management Commentary
sections.body:
The management of Infosys has emphasized the importance of its Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) program in navigating the complexities of the current business environment. As outlined in the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25, the ERM program adopts a unique approach to identify, evaluate, and mitigate risks, with a focus on secondary, consequential, and residual risks. The program also utilizes process-specific risk frameworks, intelligent risk analytics, and a technology platform, iGRC, to provide a consolidated view of risks to strategic goals. During fiscal 2025, the risk office assessed and monitored various risks, including geo-political scenarios, economic uncertainties, inflation, technology disruption, and cybersecurity, among others.

The management has also highlighted the company's financial performance, with consolidated net profit increasing from ₹26,233 crore to ₹26,713 crore, and return on net worth at 29.0% for fiscal 2025. The company's revenue growth has also shown an improvement compared to the previous fiscal year. However, the management has noted that the company's revenues are concentrated in a few geographies and client industries, and a large part of its revenue is dependent on a limited number of clients, making it vulnerable to unfavorable geo-political, economic, or health events. The company's approach to mitigating these risks is not explicitly stated in the provided excerpts, and further details can be found in the Risk Management section of the report.

sections.title: Key Risks
sections.body:
The key risks associated with Infosys are primarily driven by geo-political, macroeconomic, and health events that may impact the company's revenue and profitability. As stated in the annual report, a significant portion of the company's revenue is concentrated in a few geographies and client industries, and is dependent on a limited number of clients. Unfavorable events in these areas may result in currency volatility and reduced spend on technology products and services, ultimately impacting demand for the company's offerings. The company's risk management office has identified these risks and is working to mitigate them through various initiatives, including the implementation of a technology platform, iGRC, to provide a consolidated view of risks to strategic goals.

The company is also exposed to other risks, including cybersecurity, data protection and privacy, ESG, contractual liabilities, and a complex and evolving regulatory environment. While the company has not provided specific details on the potential financial impact of these risks, they are being closely monitored and reported on by the risk office. The company's approach to mitigating these risks includes promoting risk awareness across the organization, aggregating and accumulating exposure to risks, and using intelligent risk analytics to identify and assess potential issues. However, the exact monetary impact of these risks on the company's financials, such as revenue from operations net of GST or consolidated total, is not provided in the context.

sections.title: Bull vs Bear vs Base Case
sections.body:
The bull case for INFY is supported by its robust financial performance, with 6.1% revenue growth and a 21.1% operating margin. The company's strong cash generation capabilities, as evidenced by 44.8% free cash flow growth, and its debt-free balance sheet, with ₹54,249 crore in robust working capital, position it well for future growth. Additionally, INFY's commitment to returning approximately 85% of its free cash flow to shareholders over a five-year period through a combination of semi-annual dividends and/or share buyback/special dividends is likely to attract investors seeking steady capital returns.

The bear case, on the other hand, is less clear from the provided excerpts, as there is no explicit discussion of potential risks or downsides. However, the company's ERM framework and discussion of key and emerging risks in the Risk management section suggest that INFY is aware of potential challenges and is taking steps to mitigate them. Our base case assumes that INFY will continue to deliver solid financial performance, with revenue growth and operating margins in line with historical trends. We expect the company to maintain its strong cash generation capabilities and continue to return value to shareholders through dividends and buybacks, with the dividend per share expected to increase progressively. With a return on equity of 29.0% and a strong balance sheet, INFY is well-positioned to deliver long-term growth and create shareholder value.

The methods used to determine fair value include discounted cash flow analysis, option pricing model, market multiples, available quoted market prices and dealer quotes. All methods of assessing fair value result in general approximation of value, and such value may never actually be realized. For financial assets and liabilities maturing within one year from the Balance Sheet date and which are not carried at fair value, the carrying amounts approximates fair value due to the short maturity of these instruments. 2.11.5 Impairment The Group recognizes loss allowances using the expected credit loss (ECL) model for the financial assets and unbilled revenue which are not fair valued through profit or loss. Loss allowance for trade receivables and unbilled revenues with no significant financing component is measured at an amount equal to lifetime ECL. For all other financial assets, ECLs are measured at an amount equal to the 12-month ECL, unless there has been a significant increase in credit risk from initial recognition in which case those are measured at lifetime ECL. The Group determines the allowance for credit losses based on historical loss experience adjusted to reflect current and estimated future economic conditions. The Group considers current and anticipated future economic conditions relating to industries the Group deals with and the countries where it operates. The amount of ECL (or reversal) that is required to adjust the loss allowance at the reporting date to the amount that is required to be recorded is recognized as an impairment loss or gain in Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss. eval_context.content: Infosys Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 151 Salient features of our Enterprise Risk Management program Our ERM program adopts unique methods to identify risks, evaluate potential impact and promote risk awareness across the organization. Secondary, consequential and residual risks Secondary risks are threats that could impede the mitigation of primary risks. Consequential risks are the unintended consequences of primary mitigation, and residual risks are those risks that are left over after mitigation. Process risk frameworks Aggregation and accumulation Exposure for same risks are aggregated as it goes up the hierarchy. This provides enterprise-wide view to the leadership. Cumulated risk view is also provided to understand total exposure arising out of all risks at a unit level. Process-speciﬁc risk frameworks have been developed for decision-making, for example, frameworks for customer risk, vendor risk, contractual liability, contractual weighted risk and credit risk. Intelligent risk analytics Internal and external risk and performance indicators, and loss incidents are used in real time to identify, analyze and assess potential issues that could negatively impact strategic goals. RISC360 : iGRC Risk culture RISC360 is the Company’s Governance, Risk management and Compliance (GRC) program that combines three lines of defense under one umbrella. This enables risk-based decision-making and auditing. The Company has implemented a technology platform, iGRC, to provide a consolidated view of risks to strategic goals. Our risk culture encourages open and upward communication. Coupled with our belief systems and core values, this drives behavior, guides daily activities and decision-making throughout the organization. We encourage sharing of knowledge and best practices, continuous process improvement and a strong commitment to ethics and integrity. Enterprise Risk Management program Salient features Highlights of fiscal 2025 During fiscal 2025, various risks management initiatives were undertaken so as to ensure the smooth delivery of services to our clients, transparent communication with all stakeholders, fulfilment of our social responsibility while ensuring employee safety and health by strengthening risk management program and enhancing the risk culture. The risk office assessed, monitored and reported on risks related to geo-political scenarios; uncertainties in the economy; inflation; technology disruption and innovation; talent availability; cybersecurity; data protection and privacy; ESG; contractual liabilities; and complex and evolving regulatory environment. While the Company tracks several risks to its business, the key risks and emerging risks are described below along with the Company’s approach to mitigate them.
